subject: Urgent: Nimbus production 429s and latency — quota corridor mismatch
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike and 429s

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing a sustained increase in 5xx/429 responses and median latency is up ~3x for our production stream (us-west-2) starting at 08:50 PDT. A few request IDs attached (nimbus_request_ids.txt) — they show repeated 429s after the first successful token admission. Traffic shape hasn't changed on our side; QPS and per-request token counts are within expected ranges.

Impact: several customer-facing features are degrading, and our CS team is fielding complaints. Can you confirm whether there was a change to quota/burst rules or a service rollout that could explain forced suppression?

Attached: nimbus_sample_trace_ids.txt (list of request IDs + timestamps)

Thanks,
Elena Park
Technical Ops, Nimbus Analytics

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample IDs. We're looking into this now. I'm looping in Vivek (infra) and Laura (your account lead).

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether the traffic hit a new API route or changed model selection (e.g., longer contexts or function calls)? If not, we will attempt a temporary quota/burst override for your account to restore headroom while we root-cause.

Planned immediate action (subject to Vivek's sign-off):
- Push an account-scoped burst override (10x nominal) for 15 minutes to clear the backlog.
- Route new requests to a secondary serving pool in us-west-2 with a relaxed corridor policy.
- Collect detailed token admission logs and KV-cache metrics for the affected window.

Attached: nimbus_sample_trace_ids.txt (forwarded)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike and 429s

Marissa / Laura — quick technical update.

Root-cause hypothesis: a recent rollout of the new "quota corridor" defaults accidentally narrowed the refill window for accounts with Reserved + Hosted hybrid routing. For accounts pinned to the hybrid routing policy (Nimbus is one), the corridor multiplier was set to 0.6 during the rollout; effectively the tokenbucket refills slower under certain burst patterns and long-running sessions. That matches the pattern in the sample IDs (tokens admitted then 429s on repeated bursts).

What I'll do now:
- Stage and apply an immediate account override to set corridor multiplier to 1.2 for Nimbus for 20 minutes. This is a scoped, temporary safety action; it does not change cluster-wide defaults.
- Flip routing for new sessions to the secondary pool with an alternate kernel selection to avoid the policy path that enforces the narrow corridor.
- Collect admission logs, kernel metrics, and sequence length histograms.

Post-mitigation steps:
- Revert the rollout flag and promote a corrected default in the next canary.
- Run a targeted regression test for hybrid-routing accounts (RED-4578).
- Postmortem and credit evaluation with CS.

I'll apply the override in ~3 minutes; I'll notify once stabilised.

Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Production latency spike and 429s

Elena / Rajesh — update and next steps.

What we did (11:00 PDT):
- Applied an account-scoped corridor override for Nimbus (multiplier -> 1.2) for a 20-minute window.
- Shifted new sessions to the secondary serving pool in us-west-2.
- Enabled verbose admission logging for the affected window and created RED-4578 to track the follow-up.

Preliminary result: error rate dropped to baseline within ~7 minutes and median latency returned to normal. We will keep the override in place for the 20-minute window and then revert to monitor for recurrence.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem with engineering + CS by EOD Monday. Draft outline attached.
- We'll propose a one-time credit for the impact and walk through the corrective rollout timeline.
- Internal action: revert the rolling default and add hybrid-routing regression tests before the next canary.

Attachments: override_confirmation.txt, postmortem-outline.docx

Please confirm once your side sees restored traffic and any lingering anomalies.

Thanks for raising this quickly — we'll keep you posted every step of the way.
